intro: Every few seconds, the XRP Ledger's validators agree on a new ledger, and sign it. This page doesn't take anyone's word for it. It checks every one of those signatures itself, right here in your browser, and lights up only what passed. Light means it was checked here. An outline means someone else said so.
key: It all starts with a single key: that gold star. It belongs to the publisher of the validator list, and it's built into this page, rather than fetched from anywhere. Everything else you'll see is checked against it.
list: That key signed a list of validators: the servers the network relies on to agree. Your browser checks that signature before anything else, and then each validator's own key, vouching for the one it signs with today. Only then is the gate drawn, with one light for every validator on the list.
sigs: Every validator on the list signs every ledger. When your browser has checked one of those signatures, that validator's light comes on. And the lines beyond it are its spectrum, drawn from the very bytes it signed, so they change with every ledger. Watch them come in, one by one.
quorum: Once at least eighty percent of the validators have signed the same ledger, that's a quorum, and the network has accepted it. Just like in Deep Field, the event horizon inside the gate opens only then.
ledger: So what exactly did they sign? A fingerprint of the ledger, called a hash. Your browser computes that hash from the ledger's header itself, and compares the two. When they match, the heart of the horizon lights up, and the ledger joins the rings behind the gate: one ring for every ledger proven here since you arrived.
account: You can check any account, too. Look one up, and it appears beyond the gate as an outline: the relay's word, and nothing more. Then your browser follows that account's path through the ledger's state tree, hashing every step, all the way up to the state root in the heart. Only if it all matches does the path light up, and the account with it. Try the genesis account: the very first account the ledger ever had.
closer: There's more to find if you look closer. Turn on names, to see whose light is whose. Drag to look around the gate, and come in close. And paste in a transaction hash, to prove it and download a receipt that carries its own proof. Everything you've seen here was checked by your own browser.
